Hausman-McFadden test of IIA

Source: R/iia.R
hausman_mcfadden.Rd

For each dropped alternative, compares the multinomial logit estimated on the cases that did not choose it (restricted choice set) with the full-sample estimate of the same parameters: under IIA both are consistent and the restricted one is less efficient, so \((\hat\beta_r - \hat\beta_f)'(V_r - V_f)^{-1}(\hat\beta_r - \hat\beta_f)\) is asymptotically chi-square with as many degrees of freedom as restricted parameters (Hausman and McFadden 1984).

Usage

hausman_mcfadden(object, drop = NULL, vcov = c("difference", "joint"))

Arguments

object

A fitted mnl() model with at least three alternatives. A fit with diverging coefficients (separation) draws a warning: the contrasts then compare estimates that do not exist and can reject spuriously.

drop

Alternatives to drop, one at a time (labels or indices); default all of them.

vcov

"difference" (default) or "joint"; see Details.

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per dropped alternative: alternative, statistic, df, p.value, psd (was the covariance of the difference positive semi-definite), and n_restricted.

Details

Dropping the base alternative is handled exactly: the full model is re-expressed with the first remaining alternative as the base through the linear map \(\beta_j^{(c)} = \beta_j - \beta_c\), and the restricted model is estimated with that base, so the compared parameters coincide (the misalignment that produces spurious rejections for the base-drop row in some implementations does not arise).

vcov = "difference" is the classic form, with both covariances the inverse observed information (the form the Hausman lemma requires; the fit's own robust or cluster covariance is not used here). The difference of covariance matrices need not be positive semi-definite in finite samples; the result then reports psd = FALSE, a negative statistic is shown as computed, and its p-value is 1 (Hausman and McFadden 1984, p. 1226, and Long and Freese 2014 read a negative statistic as no evidence against IIA). A positive statistic with psd = FALSE is unreliable: in the package's size study the difference form rejected well above the nominal level. It stays the default because it is the form the literature and Stata's hausman report, so that published values can be reproduced; the joint form is the one to rely on. vcov = "joint" instead estimates the covariance of the difference from the stacked per-case scores of the two fits (the seemingly-unrelated-estimation device of Weesie 1999; Stata's mlogtest, suest): \(V_r + V_f - C - C'\) with the sandwich covariances and cross-covariance, positive semi-definite by construction and valid with heteroskedasticity and, when the fit has a cluster, clustering.

References

Hausman, J.A. and McFadden, D. (1984). Specification tests for the multinomial logit model. Econometrica, 52, 1219-1240. doi:10.2307/1910997

Weesie, J. (1999). Seemingly unrelated estimation and the cluster-adjusted sandwich estimator. Stata Technical Bulletin, 52, 34-47.

Long, J.S. and Freese, J. (2014). Regression Models for Categorical Dependent Variables Using Stata, 3rd ed. Stata Press.

See also

small_hsiao(), fp_tests(), iia_tests()

Other IIA tests: boot_pvalue(), fp_tests(), iia_tests(), nested_lm_test(), small_hsiao()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(1200, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5), d = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.9)))
m <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
hausman_mcfadden(m)
#> Hausman-McFadden test of IIA (variance difference) 
#>  alternative statistic df p.value   psd n_restricted
#>            a     7.173  6   0.305 FALSE          971
#>            b     0.027  6   1.000 FALSE          731
#>            c     1.059  6   0.983  TRUE          952
#>            d   -66.907  6   1.000 FALSE          946
#> Note: psd = FALSE: the covariance difference is not positive semi-definite. A negative statistic is no evidence against IIA (p-value 1); a positive one is unreliable (the difference form over-rejects); use vcov = "joint". 
hausman_mcfadden(m, drop = "b", vcov = "joint")
#> Hausman-McFadden test of IIA (joint (suest) covariance) 
#>  alternative statistic df p.value  psd n_restricted
#>            b     3.354  6   0.763 TRUE          731
